guide.summary: Create a Slack app using V2 OAuth (multi-workspace) via the Slack developer console. Configure redirect URLs, bot/user scopes, and install to a development workspace. Sharing the app with other workspaces via the shareable install URL ('Activate Public Distribution' under Manage Distribution) requires NO Slack review; listing in the Slack Marketplace is a separate, optional review process (up to 10 business days preliminary feedback, then up to 10 weeks functional review for new submissions).

time.approval_wait: None for development workspace; Slack Marketplace review: up to 10 business days for preliminary feedback, then up to 10 weeks for functional review of new submissions (6 weeks for published apps resubmitting changes)
time.verdict: Quick for dev install; Marketplace review wait is officially published (up to 10 business days + up to 10 weeks), not unverified.

steps.title: Sign in to Slack
steps.action: Create or sign in to your Slack account.
steps.human_because: Requires interactive login and possible MFA.
steps.nuances: Account must have access to a workspace for development. The 'Your Apps' console states: 'You'll need to sign in to your Slack account to create an application.'

steps.title: Open the Slack developer console
steps.action: Navigate to 'Your Apps' and click 'Create an app' (it links to api.slack.com/apps?new_app=1).
steps.nuances: Current docs say to select 'Blank app' then 'Continue' (not 'From scratch'); 'From a manifest' is the alternative if you have a YAML/JSON manifest.

steps.title: Create the app and select development workspace
steps.action: Enter your App Name, select the development workspace, and click 'Create'.
steps.human_because: Workspace selection and app naming are manual console steps.
steps.nuances: This workspace will be used for initial install and testing. Slack suggests a workspace 'where you won't disrupt real work getting done, like a developer sandbox'.

steps.title: Record Client ID and Client Secret
steps.action: Copy the Client ID and Client Secret from the Basic Information page, which contains 'important credentials you'll need later'. Store the secret securely; if it leaks, reset it with the 'Change secret' button.
steps.human_because: Credentials are displayed only in the authenticated console.
steps.nuances: Also note the Signing Secret for request verification. The draft's 'shown once' claim is not documented anywhere and should be dropped — Slack documents a 'Change secret' reset flow, implying the secret is not one-time-displayed.

steps.title: Configure Redirect URL(s)
steps.where: App settings → OAuth & Permissions → Redirect URLs
steps.action: Add one or more HTTPS redirect URLs. Your redirect_uri must match or be a subdirectory of a Redirect URL configured under App Management. If multiple URLs are added, the same redirect_uri must be sent in both the Authorize and Access steps (otherwise bad_redirect_uri).
steps.human_because: Console form requires manual entry and save.
steps.nuances: No HTTP, no fragments (#), no wildcards. If multiple Redirect URLs are configured but no redirect_uri is sent, 'the OAuth flow will use the first Redirect URL listed on the App Management page'. Example: https://example.com/callback or https://backend.composio.dev/api/v3/toolkits/auth/callback

steps.title: Add Bot Token Scopes and User Token Scopes
steps.action: Add required bot scopes (e.g., chat:write, commands) under 'Bot Token Scopes' and user scopes (e.g., channels:history) under 'User Token Scopes'. Add all needed scopes BEFORE installing; mark scopes optional via the app settings or bot_optional/user_optional in the manifest.
steps.human_because: Scope selection is a manual console action.
steps.nuances: SIWS scopes (openid, email, profile) must be requested in a separate OAuth flow. Users may deselect optional scopes during install; handle missing_scope errors gracefully. There is no per-scope 'Required' checkbox in the manifest — optional scopes are declared via bot_optional/user_optional arrays, which 'must also be listed in the corresponding bot/user fields'.

steps.title: Install app to development workspace
steps.where: App settings → OAuth & Permissions → Install App to Workspace
steps.action: Click 'Install App to Workspace', authorize the requested scopes, and capture the initial bot/user tokens for testing.
steps.human_because: Requires interactive authorization in the workspace.
steps.nuances: Generates xoxb- (bot) and xoxp- (user) tokens; after authorizing you land back on OAuth & Permissions to see the Bot User OAuth Access Token. No formal review needed for your own workspace (undistributed apps live on a single workspace). Scope changes require a reinstall to take effect on existing installs.

steps.title: (Optional) Define App Manifest for version control
steps.action: Create or import a YAML/JSON manifest containing scopes (oauth_config.scopes.bot/user plus bot_optional/user_optional), redirect URLs (oauth_config.redirect_urls), and token rotation settings. Enables easy replication and CI/CD.
steps.human_because: Manifest can be drafted by agent; human only needs to paste/save in console.
steps.nuances: Enable token rotation with settings.token_rotation_enabled: true (or the OAuth & Permissions toggle) — the draft's 'token_management_enabled: true' is a different oauth_config field. Rotation cannot be turned off once enabled. The Node SDK OAuth guide cited by the draft contains no manifest example; use the app manifest reference instead.

steps.title: Implement OAuth 2.0 authorization code flow (for multi-workspace distribution)
steps.action: Direct users to https://slack.com/oauth/v2/authorize with client_id, scope, user_scope (optional), redirect_uri, state. Exchange the returned code (10-min lifetime) at https://slack.com/api/oauth.v2.access with client_id, client_secret, code, and redirect_uri (send the same value in both Authorize and Access steps when multiple redirect URLs are configured). Validate state — a mismatch means 'consider the authorization a forgery'. Store per-workspace/enterprise installation data (team.id, enterprise.id, is_enterprise_install, tokens).
steps.human_because: Code implementation can be automated; human reviews and deploys.
steps.nuances: If no redirect_uri is sent, Slack uses the first Redirect URL listed under App Management; redirect_uri is required in the token exchange only if it was sent in the authorize step. SIWS scopes require a separate flow. Token rotation uses refresh tokens when enabled (access tokens then expire every 12 hours and carry an xoxe. prefix).

steps.title: (Optional) Share the app for public install — no review needed
steps.where: App settings → Manage Distribution → Activate Public Distribution
steps.action: Complete the distribution checklist (working OAuth 2.0 flow, SSL for all request URLs, only the permissions you need) and activate public distribution to get a shareable install URL and an embeddable 'Add to Slack' button.
steps.human_because: Checklist sign-off and activation are manual console actions.
steps.nuances: Unlisted distribution does NOT require Slack review — Slack calls it 'perfect for when you want to test out your app by running a pilot for early customers'. Slack review applies only to Slack Marketplace listing (directory presence).

steps.title: (Optional) Submit to Slack Marketplace for directory listing
steps.where: App settings → 'Submit to the Slack Marketplace' section
steps.action: Meet the prerequisites (app installed on 10+ active workspaces, fully tested including uninstalling it, privacy policy, publicly accessible support page, per-scope justifications, video demo of the full install/OAuth flow), then submit for review.
steps.human_because: Legal documents, scope justification, and submission require human decisions.
steps.nuances: Apps under 10 installed active workspaces 'will be blocked from submitting'. Preliminary review feedback 'generally takes up to 10 business days'; functional review takes 'up to 10 weeks for new submissions and 6 weeks for published apps resubmitting changes'. After approval you publish at a time of your choosing; the live version is locked until changes are resubmitted.

gotchas.title: Redirect URI strict matching
gotchas.why_it_matters: Slack requires the redirect_uri to match or be a subdirectory of a configured Redirect URL; no wildcards, no HTTP, no fragments (#). Mismatch causes a bad_redirect_uri error.
gotchas.how_to_handle: Register the precise HTTPS callback URL (e.g., https://backend.composio.dev/api/v3/toolkits/auth/callback). If multiple URLs, send identical redirect_uri in both Authorize and Access requests. If none is sent, Slack falls back to the first Redirect URL listed under App Management.

gotchas.title: Authorization code expires in 10 minutes
gotchas.why_it_matters: The code returned from the authorization redirect is 'your temporary authorization code, which expires after ten minutes' and must be exchanged at oauth.v2.access within that window.
gotchas.how_to_handle: Exchange the code immediately in your callback handler; implement retry/queue if needed.

gotchas.title: SIWS scopes cannot be mixed with bot/user scopes
gotchas.why_it_matters: 'A scope conflict occurs when attempting to combine Sign in with Slack (SIWS) user scopes with non-Sign in with Slack scopes in the same OAuth flow' and 'Each set of scopes must be requested in a separate OAuth flow' (invalid_scope error).
gotchas.how_to_handle: Run a separate OAuth flow for Sign in with Slack using only SIWS scopes (openid, email, profile).

gotchas.title: Optional scopes may be deselected by user
gotchas.why_it_matters: Optional scopes (bot_optional/user_optional in the manifest) are presented to the installer, 'who can choose which ones to grant'; your app must handle missing scopes gracefully.
gotchas.how_to_handle: Check the scope field in the token response to see which scopes were granted; gate features accordingly and handle missing_scope errors.

gotchas.title: Token rotation requires secure refresh token storage
gotchas.why_it_matters: When token rotation is enabled, access tokens expire every 12 hours (expires_in is always 43,200 seconds) and carry an xoxe. prefix; refresh tokens are single-use and 'revoked after a short grace period'; Slack enforces a limit of 2 active tokens. Rotation 'may not be turned off once it's turned on'.
gotchas.how_to_handle: Enable via settings.token_rotation_enabled: true in the manifest or the OAuth & Permissions toggle. Store refresh tokens encrypted; refresh via oauth.v2.access with grant_type=refresh_token (initial conversion of a legacy token uses oauth.v2.exchange).

gotchas.title: Localhost testing requires HTTPS
gotchas.why_it_matters: The current OAuth V2 docs state 'The redirect_uri must use HTTPS' with no localhost exception; only the legacy Sign-in-with-Slack docs allowed plain-http localhost redirects.
gotchas.how_to_handle: Use ngrok, cloudflared, or a local HTTPS proxy (e.g., mkcert) to expose https://localhost:port.

gotchas.title: Scope changes require reinstall; scopes can be added but never downgraded
gotchas.why_it_matters: 'Some manifest changes, such as adding scopes, only take effect for existing installs after workspaces reinstall your app.' Scopes cannot be removed from a live token: 'It is not possible to downgrade an access token's scopes' — removal requires revoking the token.
gotchas.how_to_handle: Finalize scopes before install. After adding scopes, reinstall in each workspace. Read the granted scopes from the token response and gate features rather than assuming all requested scopes are live.

blockers.issue: Marketplace review wait is long and now officially published (no longer unknown)
blockers.how_to_resolve: Plan for up to 10 business days of preliminary feedback plus up to 10 weeks of functional review for new submissions (6 weeks for resubmissions). The app must be installed on 10 or more active workspaces before submitting or it 'will be blocked from submitting'; prepare the video demo, privacy policy, public support page, and per-scope justifications first.
blockers.escalation: Feedback arrives in the submission flow and via email; address all feedback and resubmit. Note that resubmitting during preliminary review resets your queue position.

blockers.issue: OAuth endpoint rate limits are only partially documented
blockers.how_to_resolve: oauth.v2.access documents a rate limit of 600 requests per minute (tier t5, 'Special rate limits apply'); no published limit exists for the oauth/v2/authorize endpoint. Implement exponential backoff and respect Retry-After headers; monitor for 429 responses.
blockers.escalation: File a support ticket if consistent rate limiting blocks legitimate traffic.

sources.title: Installing with OAuth (redirects from api.slack.com/authentication/oauth-v2)
sources.what_it_supports: OAuth V2 endpoints, redirect_uri match/subdirectory rules, HTTPS requirement, no fragments, first-URL fallback, same redirect_uri in Authorize+Access, 10-minute code expiry, xoxb/xoxp tokens, state validation, SIWS scope conflict, optional scopes, scope downgrade prohibition, org-level installs needing Org Owner/Admin

sources.title: App lifecycle & distribution
sources.what_it_supports: Three distribution options (single workspace, unlisted public distribution, Slack Marketplace); unlisted distribution via 'Activate Public Distribution' needs NO review; Marketplace listing is reviewed; distribution checklist (OAuth flow, SSL URLs)

sources.title: Slack Marketplace review process
sources.what_it_supports: Submission from 'Submit to the Slack Marketplace' section; 10+ active workspaces prerequisite; preliminary review up to 10 business days; functional review up to 10 weeks (new) / 6 weeks (resubmit); video demo; publish-after-approval; live app locked; return-and-resubmit process

sources.title: Submission guidelines and requirements
sources.what_it_supports: Privacy policy, public support page (2-business-day response), scope justifications, 10 active workspaces / 20 MAU suitability threshold, ToS agreements for Marketplace distribution, no formal appeal described, resubmission after substantial changes

sources.title: Updated installation requirement for Slack Marketplace apps
sources.what_it_supports: As of July 2026 apps need at least 10 installations on active workspaces, maintained throughout the entire review
